_comment: Runtime limits for SAS_Parser. null means 'unset' (the code default applies). Precedence: explicit constructor argument > this file > code default. Loaded via the app_config package; point SAS_PARSER_CONFIG at an alternative file to override.
_prompt_builder_comment: 'max_instruction_tokens' is the total TOKEN budget for the per-item guidance block, shared by operator rules and retrieved reference chunks; the selector fills it in priority order and drops whole chunks at the tail. Tokens, not words: measured over the bundled reference corpus the tokens-per-word ratio runs 1.01 to 4.41 (median 1.44) depending on how much of a section is code, so a word budget silently under-counted exactly the SQL-heavy guidance this set is made of. BREAKING: the old 'max_instruction_words' key is gone -- app_config raises if it is still present rather than reverting to a default. 14000 is the measured zero-drop point: over a 70-line reference program batching into two items, every rule those items' constructs matched arrives, the items draw 12.4k tokens, and more budget buys nothing (8000 dropped 7 rules, 10000 dropped 4). Pair it with user_instructions.max_tokens 9800 (70%). It is a ceiling, not a cost floor -- every section is scoped to a construct the item actually uses, so a simple DATA step draws far less no matter how high this is set. Keep it >= instruction_chunker.max_tokens so one reference section always fits.
_llm_client_comment: The AI Gateway. 'gateway_version' is sent as the 'ai-gateway-version' header on every request ('v2' for the current gateway); an explicit url_headers entry of the same name wins. 'model_provider' names the family the gateway routes to ('anthropic', 'openai', ...) and is also filled in from a 'provider: model' prefix on 'model'. 'provider_client' picks how the chat model is built: 'auto' (the default) lets 'model_provider' decide, exactly as the reference deployment does against this same gateway -- 'anthropic' routes to the native client, 'openai' and 'google' to the OpenAI-compatible one, and a named-but-unrecognised provider is an error rather than a guess. 'openai_compatible' pins the LangChain ChatOpenAI everything here is written around -- retry with Retry-After, the input-token budget, prompt-cache breakpoints, structured output; 'native' pins the raw openai SDK for a gateway that will not take the LangChain payload, and gives up every construction-time feature (rate limiter, model_kwargs, structured output -- for which notebook rendering already falls back to parsing the Markdown response). An explicit value always wins over the provider, in either direction; a model id with no provider on it takes 'openai_compatible'. 'roles' holds SPARSE overlays: a key a role does not mention resolves from this section, so 'validator' and 'complexity' differ only where they say they do.
_pipeline_comment: Pipeline behaviour. 'structured_output' asks the model for a typed TranslationDocument (analysis / mapping / ordered notebook cells / risks) instead of free-form Markdown, so pipeline.notebook knows which cells are runnable code rather than guessing from fences. The turn persisted to memory and the item's 'response' stay Markdown either way, so conversation memory, resume, and validation are unaffected; a gateway that will not honour the schema degrades to the model's prose with a warning. Set false to prompt for plain Markdown. 'max_merged_tokens' bounds token-budgeted call packing: adjacent work items (independent singletons AND small dependency batches) share one LLM call while the estimated prompt cost stays under this many tokens, cutting per-call overhead. null derives a default (packing is ON by default: 0.8 x the input-token headroom when llm_client.max_input_tokens is set, else ~64000); set 0 to turn packing off (count-capped singleton merging only). Item ids change under packing (packed-NNN), so resume only matches runs made under the same budget.
_pipeline_language_comment: 'output_language' resolves once for every run and controls prompting, instruction selection, notebook metadata, validation, complexity, and XREF. Supported targets are PySpark and Spark SQL. Spelling is folded, so SparkSQL, spark sql, spark_sql, sql, and Spark SQL select Spark SQL. Unsupported names fail before conversion. null uses the code default (Spark SQL); an explicit pipeline or CLI value wins over this file, while a SharePoint request row wins for its request.
_complexity_comment: Complexity analysis. 'target' names a rule-set profile under complexity/profiles/ ('sparksql', 'pyspark', ...); 'rules_path' points at a profile file of your own and wins over 'target'. The per-tier weights only rank units within a tier; they can never change a tier, which is presence-based (any HIGH construct makes the unit HIGH). Retune which construct maps to which tier by editing a profile JSON, not here.
_complexity_sizing_comment: T-shirt sizing (S/M/L/XL per source file). Each of the three dimensions (effort, complexity, uncertainty) is log-transformed and min-max rescaled onto 0-1 against a window declared in the profile as a MULTIPLE of the anchor, then blended by the profile's dimension weights, then rescaled in log space onto the 2-8 point Fibonacci scale. 'size_anchor' is the raw score of the reference MEDIUM file that every window is stated against, so LOWERING it makes every file rate LARGER. 'min_story_points'/'max_story_points' re-denominate the reported points onto your own scale (e.g. 1 and 13 instead of the Fibonacci 2 and 8); they change the NUMBERS only, never a size, because the bands are read as fractions of the span. The rest of the calibration -- band boundaries, min-max bounds, per-dimension weights -- lives in the profile's 'sizes' block; only these knobs are exposed here because they move every verdict coherently. 'use_cross_file' resolves each file's macro/dataset/macro-variable/libref references against the rest of the corpus; turning it off scores every file as if it were the only one.
_user_instructions_comment: Operator translation rules injected per item. 'dir' is a directory of *.md files whose first path component names the target language ('sparksql/', or '_common/' for language-agnostic); it takes precedence over the single-file 'path'. README*.md and _-prefixed files are documentation and are never ingested. 'dir' ships pointing at the bundled starter set, which is scoped [lang: sparksql] and therefore inert under any other output_language; set it to null to inject no operator rules, or to your own directory to use project conventions instead. WARNING: that set targets DATABRICKS SQL - it uses QUALIFY, SQL scripting, EXECUTE IMMEDIATE, UNPIVOT and three-level catalog.schema.table names, which open-source Spark does not have. Point 'dir' elsewhere if you run a non-Databricks Spark. A relative value is resolved against the repo root when it does not exist relative to the working directory, so the default survives being run from elsewhere.'max_tokens' caps operator rules and examples inside prompt_builder.max_instruction_tokens so they cannot starve the reference corpus; null means uncapped, which is fine for a handful of rules but not for a large set - uncapped rules simply consume the whole budget. It is set to 70% of max_instruction_tokens, which leaves ~1050 words for reference chunks; move the two together if you change either.
_validation_comment: Per-metric pass thresholds; null uses the metric class default. language_compliance scores whether emitted code blocks use the selected target, and target_syntax verifies them with Python AST for PySpark or sqlglot under the Databricks dialect for Spark SQL. Every metric is higher-is-better. The LLM-judged thresholds are inert unless that suite is enabled.
_spark_comment: Where the Spark cluster is. 'master' is the URL a SparkSession is built against when the caller does not pass one -- the Delta memory backend (memory.store) and validation tracking. Also read from SPARK_MASTER_URL, which wins over this file; the Docker stack sets it on the app service, so the compose cluster is used without changing anything here. null uses the code default, 'local[*]' (an in-process cluster), which is also what a bare-metal run gets when nothing is configured. Note that this value overrides spark.master in $SPARK_CONF_DIR/spark-defaults.conf, because an explicit builder.master() call outranks that file.
_vault_comment: Non-secret Vault connection settings only. Secrets (VAULT_TOKEN, VAULT_ROLE_ID, VAULT_SECRET_ID) come from the environment, never this file. address/namespace/auth_path/app_name/azure_scopes also read from VAULT_ADDR/VAULT_NAMESPACE/VAULT_AUTH_PATH/VAULT_APP_NAME/VAULT_AZURE_SCOPES, which win over these. app_name is ONE value playing three parts, exactly as the reference deployment uses it: the Vault role name, the KV secret-path prefix, and the application's own name. Setting it enables 'azuread' login: an Entra ID JWT (see 'azure' and databricks.secret_scope) is presented to the jwt auth method at auth/<auth_path>/login. azure_scopes is the audience that JWT is minted for; null requests Azure Resource Manager (https://management.azure.com//.default -- the doubled slash is ARM's documented form), which is what a role bound to the ARM audience expects. ai_gateway_path defaults to '<app_name>/ai_gateway'; ai_gateway_key names the field holding the token in it, and null tries token/api_key/apikey/ai_gateway_token/value in order.
_databricks_comment: Non-secret Databricks workspace settings only. The token (DATABRICKS_TOKEN) and service-principal secret (ARM_CLIENT_SECRET) come from the environment, never this file. DATABRICKS_* values and ARM_TENANT_ID/ARM_CLIENT_ID override this file. Set azure_workspace_resource_id only when the service principal is not assigned to the workspace. secret_scope names the Databricks scope holding the service-principal and SharePoint credentials.
_azure_comment: Non-secret Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD) settings only. The client secret (AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET) comes from the environment, never this file. tenant_id/client_id/authority_host/scopes/certificate_* also read from AZURE_TENANT_ID/AZURE_CLIENT_ID/AZURE_AUTHORITY_HOST/AZURE_SCOPES/AZURE_CLIENT_CERTIFICATE_PATH/AZURE_CLIENT_CERTIFICATE_THUMBPRINT, which win over these. flow: 'client_credentials' (service principal) or 'device_code' (interactive user login); null infers it from the credentials present. 'verify' is TLS verification for the Entra ID call itself (true, false, or a path to a CA bundle) and matters on a TLS-intercepting network, where the token request fails before Vault is ever contacted; null inherits vault.verify, since one bundle normally covers both legs. 'proxies' is an optional {scheme: url} mapping handed straight to MSAL. Also read from AZURE_VERIFY.
_sharepoint_comment: Non-secret SharePoint (Microsoft Graph) settings only. There is no secret here. Identify the site with site_id, or site_hostname + site_path; drive_id targets a specific document library (default: the site's). Every key is also read from its SHAREPOINT_* env var, which wins over this file.
_sharepoint_auth_comment: SharePoint authenticates as its OWN service principal, not the 'azure' one that reaches Vault: same Databricks secret scope, different keys. secret_scope defaults to databricks.secret_scope, and tenant_id_key/client_id_key/client_secret_key default to saact-hsv-tenantid/saact-hsv-appid/saact-hsv-secret. Leave all four null unless the deployment files that principal somewhere else. When no scope is configured at all, the 'azure' identity is used instead, which is the local/dev path.
_sharepoint_paths_comment: file_server_base_path is the applications root, DRIVE-relative: a leading 'Shared Documents/' is stripped on load, because Graph addresses items inside the library and a literal folder of that name does not exist. The four list ids drive the run -- requests, conversions, the XREF table, and complexity requests. A flow that needs an id which is not set fails naming the key rather than sending null to Graph.
_xref_comment: Dataset-name cross-reference: the SharePoint XREF list maps schema.table to catalog.schema.table. pre rewrites SAS metadata before conversion; post parses generated Spark SQL with sqlglot under the Databricks dialect or PySpark with AST; both reports names reached only after conversion. on_parse_failure is warn or error. sqlglot is a required dependency.
